title: DEL-1 is an endogenous senolytic protein that inhibits senescence-associated bone loss 9361
abstract:
Accumulation of senescent cells in the bone microenvironment, including bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs), contributes to aging-related bone degeneration and chronic inflammation. We herein describe DEL-1, the expression of which declines in old age, as an endogenous secreted senolytic protein. DEL-1 promoted apoptosis of senescent BMSCs via a β3 integrin/CD73/adenosine/p38 MAPK pathway, thereby leading to their clearance by macrophages. DEL-1-deficiency displayed increased abundance of β3 integrin-rich CD73+ senescent BMSCs and higher chemotherapy-induced or aging-related senescence-associated bone loss and inflammation. Conversely, mice with endothelial-specific overexpression of DEL-1 (EC-Del1) had decreased numbers of senescent BMSCs and diminished senescence-associated bone loss. CD73-deficiency reversed the reduction in senescent BMSC numbers in EC-Del1 mice. Administration of DEL-1 (or a DEL-1-inducing macrolide) caused a reduction in senescence markers and reversed aging-related periodontitis. Therefore, DEL-1 may be harnessed as an endogenous senolytic to prevent senescent cell buildup, mitigate inflammation, and senescence-associated bone loss.
